clue.text: Rarely dancing on ice with an Elvis number?

indicators.note: dancing letters jig about into a new order, so on ice and an are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, anagram fodder
taken as written, anagram fodder
Blue Moon is a song Elvis Presley recorded

explanation.surface: A rare sight: a figure skater performing to an Elvis Presley song.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dancing' rearranges ON ICE plus AN into ONCE IN A; 'with' just joins on the Elvis song.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means hardly ever, a blue moon being an unusual second full moon in one month.

clue.text: Did rock and roll material, by the sound of it

indicators.note: tells us the material's name is only heard, giving a word spelt differently

parts.note: suede is a soft leather material

explanation.surface: Seems to describe a fabric associated with rock and roll, like Blue Suede Shoes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rock and roll' looks like the music genre, but here both words are verbs for moving to and fro.
explanation.definitionFit: To rock and to roll both mean moving from side to side, which is what swaying is.

clue.text: Maybe GI initially dropping bit of litter

indicators.note: says the opening letter of the soldier word falls away

parts.note: a grunt is American slang for an infantry soldier, a GI being one example

explanation.surface: A soldier dropping litter, perhaps getting told off for it.
explanation.walkthrough: A GRUNT is US slang for a foot soldier, just as GI is.
explanation.definitionFit: The runt is the smallest animal born in a litter of puppies or piglets.

clue.text: Angriest when provoked, one won't react and isn't noble

definitions.text: one won't react and isn't noble

indicators.note: a provoked person is stirred up, so the letters of angriest are stirred into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Someone who stays calm even when provoked, though not out of nobility.
explanation.walkthrough: Nitrogen is commonly called an inert gas but is not one of the noble gases, hence the playful definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A chemically unreactive gas such as nitrogen is described this way without belonging to the noble group of elements.

clue.text: Chinese dog flips, displaying neurosis

parts.note: the Han are the majority ethnic group of China

indicators.note: flipping something turns it over, so the dog's name is read backwards

parts.note: a pug is a small breed of dog

explanation.surface: A Chinese breed of dog doing somersaults, showing it is anxious.
explanation.definitionFit: A hang-up is an emotional problem or fixation, an informal word for a neurosis.

clue.text: Arrest Charlie, poking e.g. Saudi in row improperly

parts.note: to arrest a suspect is to catch them

indicators.note: Charlie pokes into the middle of the Saudi word, sitting inside it

parts.note: a Saudi is an example of an Arab
Charlie is C in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Police arresting someone after a fight in which a Saudi was poked during a row.
explanation.walkthrough: 'row' suggests a quarrel but means rowing a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: In rowing, to catch a crab is to fumble a stroke so the oar jams in the water.

clue.text: In France, plonk date on potato dish from India

parts.note: vin is French for wine; plonk is cheap wine
aloo is the Hindi word for potato, used on Indian menus

explanation.surface: A French diner drops cheap wine onto an Indian potato curry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' simply joins the pieces; in a down clue the date sits on top of the potato.
explanation.definitionFit: Vindaloo is a fiery curry that originated in Goa on India's west coast.

clue.text: Bar's saving pounds in charge account for promotional activity

indicators.note: saving here means keeping safe within, so the bar word holds the rest

parts.note: a pub is a bar; with the 's this gives PUBS
L stands for pounds, from the Latin libra
a relation is an account or narrative of events

explanation.surface: A pub saving money by keeping a tab running in its accounts.
explanation.definitionFit: PR is the business of managing a firm's public image through publicity.

clue.text: Island city rejected old money

indicators.note: something rejected is thrown back, so the city word is read backwards

parts.note: a wen is an old word for an overcrowded city, as in London's Great Wen
the guinea was a British gold coin worth 21 shillings

explanation.surface: A city turning down old currency.
explanation.walkthrough: The Great Wen was William Cobbett's nickname for London.
explanation.definitionFit: New Guinea is the large Pacific landmass north of Australia, the world's second largest.

clue.text: Item getting rolled gold on the outside is so long

indicators.note: says the gold symbol wraps around the outside of the item

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold
a die is an object you roll in board games

explanation.surface: Something rolled up in gold leaf being described as very long.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are farewells: 'so long' is an informal goodbye and the French word is another.

clue.text: State of discomfort accepted by otherworldly figure

indicators.note: being accepted by means being taken in, so the discomfort goes inside

parts.note: ET is the alien from Spielberg's film
gyp is British slang for pain or discomfort, as in 'my knee's giving me gyp'

explanation.surface: An alien putting up with some discomfort.
explanation.definitionFit: Egypt is a country, and 'state' here means a nation.

clue.text: Wasting sovereign and coppers on serving man wearing Spanish outfit

indicators.note: the Spanish club has the other pieces on, like clothing, so they go inside

parts.note: Real Madrid is a Spanish football team, an outfit being a team

indicators.note: in an across clue, coppers on the serving man means the police come after him

parts.note: a GI is an American serviceman
CID is the Criminal Investigation Department, British police detectives

explanation.surface: Throwing away gold coins and pennies on a waiter in a Spanish costume.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wasting' is slang for killing, and 'sovereign' and 'coppers' both pretend to be coins.
explanation.definitionFit: Regicide is the killing of a monarch, so the adjective describes a king-killing act.

clue.text: No good drinking rum, cool like Homer 1 Down?

indicators.note: something drinking takes liquid in, so the no-good letters hold the others

parts.note: rum means odd or strange
in means fashionable, cool

explanation.surface: A bad idea to drink rum while trying to stay calm like Homer.
explanation.walkthrough: The proverb 'even Homer nods' means even the greatest poet slips up, and 1 Down says only rarely.
explanation.definitionFit: Homer, the epic poet, supposedly nods off only now and then, so the word describes his rare lapses.

clue.text: Cow, one I see eating wild mint

indicators.note: the outer letters eat the shuffled mint, taking it in

parts.note: one is I in Roman numerals
to see someone is to date them

indicators.note: wild letters run free into a new order, so mint is rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Watching a cow munch on wild mint in a field.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cow' looks like the animal from the surface but is the verb meaning to bully; 'see' means go out with.
explanation.definitionFit: To cow someone is to frighten them into submission, a verb meaning to bully.

clue.text: Image captures prince left looking like a plonker

indicators.note: the image word captures the others, holding them inside

parts.note: pic is short for picture, an image
Prince Hal is the young Henry V in Shakespeare

explanation.surface: A photo shows a royal leaving, looking a fool.
explanation.walkthrough: A plonker is British slang for an idiot, but also for a penis.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means shaped like a penis, and plonker is vulgar British slang for one.

clue.text: Second old conservative admitted to feeling we're making no progress

parts.note: to second a motion is to back it

indicators.note: the old conservative is let into the feeling word, placed inside it

parts.note: tone is a feeling or mood
a square is a conventional, old-fashioned person

explanation.surface: A traditionalist feels stuck going nowhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Second' is the verb, to back a proposal, not a unit of time or second place.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means returning to the start after failing, so all progress is lost.

clue.text: Sega ultimately crashed, playing game

indicators.note: playing about with letters means mixing them into a new order
ultimately points to the final letter of Sega

parts.note: taken as written, anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A Sega console crashing while someone is playing a game.
explanation.definitionFit: Charades is a party game in which players mime words for others to guess.

clue.text: Take seat from empty, unclean Sierra and go off

indicators.note: an empty word has its insides removed, leaving only its first and last letters

parts.note: Sierra is S in the NATO phonetic alphabet
eggs that addle go bad, go off

explanation.surface: Someone cleaning a seat before driving off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seat' suggests a chair, but here it is a saddle.
explanation.definitionFit: To unsaddle a horse is to remove its saddle, the rider's seat.

clue.text: Perhaps not dangerous, or safe in the East End

indicators.note: Cockneys of London's East End drop their aitches, so the H goes

parts.note: unharmed means safe, unhurt

explanation.surface: Wondering whether some London neighbourhood is risky or safe.
explanation.walkthrough: The East End is a working-class district of London where the dropped H is a stock feature of the accent.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone without weapons usually poses little threat, hence 'perhaps' in the definition.

clue.text: Frustrate artist plugging song the wrong way

indicators.note: the artist plugs a gap, sitting inside the song
running the wrong way means read backwards

parts.note: a lied is a German art song
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: An artist annoyed at a song being promoted badly.
explanation.walkthrough: A lied (plural lieder) is a German art song, a word crosswords often use for song.
explanation.definitionFit: To derail a plan is to wreck its progress, as a train leaves its rails.

clue.text: Southern peninsula is a notoriously chilly place

parts.note: Iberia is the peninsula of Spain and Portugal

explanation.surface: Claiming a southern European peninsula is famously cold.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is absurd because Iberia is warm; the S changes everything.
explanation.definitionFit: The Russian region is famed for bitterly cold winters and for the prison camps sent there.

clue.text: Vermouth's knocked back after caviare? It's on the menu in Switzerland

definitions.text: It's on the menu in Switzerland

indicators.note: the vermouth piece comes after the fish eggs in the answer

parts.note: caviare is fish roe

indicators.note: knocked back means turned backwards, so the vermouth word is reversed

parts.note: It is short for Italian vermouth, as in gin and It; with the 's this gives ITS

explanation.surface: Downing a vermouth after caviare in a Swiss restaurant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knocked back' looks like drinking the vermouth but is the reversal signal; It is Italian vermouth, as in gin and It.
explanation.definitionFit: Rösti is a Swiss dish of grated fried potato, a national speciality.

clue.text: Doctor named drug, having inflamed wound

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so the letters of named are altered

parts.note: taken as written, anagram fodder
E is slang for the drug ecstasy
inflamed skin is red

explanation.surface: A doctor names a drug for a patient with an inflamed injury.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wound' is not an injury but the past tense of wind; 'Doctor' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A river that meandered wound its way along a twisting course.

clue.text: Ancient Gaul's cut by daggers

indicators.note: cut means trimmed, losing its final letter

parts.note: Obelix is the ancient Gaul in the Asterix comics; 's reads as 'is'

explanation.surface: A Gaul in ancient times being stabbed by daggers.
explanation.definitionFit: The obelus is the dagger symbol used in printing to mark footnotes; this is its plural.

clue.text: E.g. Napoleon's comment suggesting why tattoo is impossible

definitions.meaning: first sense: the noise of a pig, Napoleon being Orwell's porcine dictator
second sense: read as zero plus a word for tattoo pigment, there is nothing to tattoo with

explanation.surface: Napoleon remarking on why getting a tattoo cannot happen.
explanation.walkthrough: Napoleon is the pig in Orwell's Animal Farm, not the emperor.
explanation.definitionFit: A pig's grunting noise, which is what the porcine leader would utter.

clue.text: Plain with nothing green in Quebec, perhaps

parts.note: O looks like zero, nothing
vert is French for green, spoken in Quebec

explanation.surface: A Canadian prairie with no greenery at all.
explanation.definitionFit: Overt means open and obvious, just as plain does when something is clear to see.

clue.text: Working in gilts with working capital, partly

indicators.note: working letters are being worked over into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, anagram fodder
on means functioning, working

explanation.surface: A City trader working with gilt-edged bonds and working capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' is not money but London, and the answer is part of it.
explanation.definitionFit: Islington is a borough of London, so it forms one part of the UK capital.
